uses.binding: Pairs of letter names English speakers confuse: e/i, g/j, a/e, r/erre; learner taps the letter heard, then says each so a partner can tell them apart
Hear a letter name and tap the letter card; younger learners point instead of writing
Vowel minimal pairs peso/piso/paso, mesa/misa, todo/toda; learner picks what was heard, then records each so a listener can tell them apart
Learner records "chocolate", "teléfono", "leche", transcribes what a Spanish listener would hear, flags any vowel reduced to schwa
Hear spelled names and emails and type them into form fields; check h, b/v, ll, tildes and @ are right
Learner lacks a partner's surname and email and must get them with ¿Cómo se escribe? and check by reading back
Greeting–how-are-you–goodbye turns; branches by clock time (9:00 / 16:00 / 22:00) check that the greeting matches the time and that the learner asks back
Hola, ¿qué tal? to a classmate vs Buenos días, ¿cómo está? to an older neighbour; learner marks which one sounds too casual
Short incidents (bump into someone, receive help, toast at dinner); learner picks the formula and the reply; branch shows reaction to lo siento vs perdón

Directions or price exchange where the partner speaks too fast; branch only continues after a repair phrase
Short clips of gestures (así así, shh, watch-glance); learner says what the speaker meant and what reply fits

Three-sentence text about a family; learner links each dropped subject to the right person
Learner fills the ser grid, then applies it to new subjects (mi madre y yo, Pedro y tú); each step shows which person the form encodes

Country shown, learner types masculine and feminine nationality before the answer appears; first attempt kept
Rule -o/-a vs consonant + a vs invariable; apply to unseen nationalities (portugués, japonés, belga)
Party scene: learner introduces themself, then a friend to a third person; branch checks este/esta and encantado/a against the characters
Same introduction to a classmate (Este es…) and to a new boss (Le presento a la señora…); learner flags the mismatched version
Same question to a child, a classmate, a hotel receptionist and an elderly neighbour; learner sets tú/usted and checks verb form agrees
Sentences where only the verb ending shows tú vs usted (¿Habla inglés? / ¿Hablas inglés?); learner decides who is being addressed

Grid of situations × countries (Spain, Mexico, Argentina): learner predicts kisses/handshake, then compares with the provided notes

Minimal pairs of melody only (Es tarde. / ¿Es tarde?); learner must produce the version a partner identifies

Sentences where the position of ¿ changes what is asked (Y tú, ¿vienes? / ¿Y tú vienes?); learner places it

Same picture story: learner chooses un/el for each mention and sees how the meaning (new vs already known) changes
Sentences where only the article tells whether the listener knows the object (¿Tienes un bolígrafo? / ¿Tienes el bolígrafo?)
Agreement rule for -o, -e and consonant adjectives; apply to unseen adjective–noun pairs (una calle ancha, unos coches azules)
Describe a picture of a street; check each adjective agrees with the noun it is attached to and matches the picture
Scene with speaker, listener and objects at three distances; learner moves the speaker and must re-choose este/ese/aquel
Hear "Dame ese libro" etc. and tap the object at the right distance from the speaker

Lost-property picture with coloured objects; learner describes one, partner identifies it; check colour, size and agreement
Object picture shown; learner types the noun with article and a colour before the answer appears

Group photo: learner describes one person; elements (pelo, gafas, altura, ropa) are checked against the picture
Feature cards: learner must choose ser / tener / llevar by meaning (alto, gafas, el pelo rizado, barba)

Sentences without subjects; learner must say who acts using only the verb ending

Pairs Lava el perro / Se lava; learner chooses which picture each sentence describes
Picture strip of a morning; learner orders it and retells with reflexive verbs and times
Announcements and conversations with times; learner fills a schedule; errors grouped by y/menos, cuarto/media, 12/24-hour
A real bus timetable and shop opening hours; learner finds the time needed to make a plan

Weekly planner page: learner fills in days and dates; check lower case and day–number–de–month order
Timeline with today, tomorrow and Saturday; learner places sentences (Mañana trabajo / Trabajo los lunes) as plan or habit

Picture strip of a day; learner orders it, then retells using primero/después/luego; check every picture is mentioned in order

ir and venir grids, then new subjects; irregular forms highlighted

Friend tells weekend news; learner keeps it going with echo questions and ¿De verdad?
Sentences where only the spelling (por qué / porque) shows question or answer; learner chooses

Objects (abrebotellas, paraguas, llave); learner explains each with es para + infinitive

Postcard and text-message templates; each slot (lugar, tiempo, actividad, despedida) constrains what is written

Photo of a room or person; learner writes a description; elements in the picture are checked (mentioned, position, number, colour)

Short announcements and dialogues; only the target slots are recorded; errors classified by number, time or name

After the model, learner writes three real plans of their own and checks which chunks transferred
